Welcome to Growth Talk. Today my guest is Marcela, a growth consultant from Brazil. Marcela, what is the biggest trend right now?
Thanks, Josh. For me, it is AI search. Many people ask a chatbot now, not Google. If brands don’t prepare for that, they will lose brand awareness.
Interesting. I have a small company. What will happen if I do nothing?
Honestly? If you do nothing, your competitors will appear in the answers, and you won’t.
OK, that is scary. And personalization? Everybody talks about it.
It is powerful, but be careful with privacy. If customers feel watched, they won’t trust the brand.
So, can you predict one thing for the next five years?
One thing: loyalty will be more valuable than traffic. If you keep your customers, you will grow.
For me, the biggest trend is AI search.
If you keep your customers, you will grow.
Nobody can predict the future, but data helps.

Hello, and welcome back to the book corner. Today's book is Quantum Marketing, by Raja Rajamannar, a marketing leader at Mastercard. The main message is simple: marketing is changing very fast, and the old methods will not be enough. The author talks about new channels, about data, and about artificial intelligence. He also talks a lot about trust. If brands use customer data without care, people will stop trusting them. My opinion? It is a good book for managers. It is not a very technical book, so you can read it on a weekend. But one idea stays with me: if marketers don't learn about technology, they will be left behind.

Hi, it's Katrin again. My director asked me: what will CRM look like in five years? Here are my three predictions. First, emails will be more personal. Every customer will get a different message, at a different time. Second, we will send fewer messages. If customers get too many emails, they will unsubscribe, and they won't come back. So less is more. Third, chatbots. They will answer the simple questions, day and night. But for a problem, people will still want to talk to people. If a brand forgets that, it will lose loyalty. Of course, I can't predict the future. But the data tells a story.
